This is the third time I've traced this exact same gate failure to the same root cause, and it is not something I can fix without leaving my task's `covers`. Stating that plainly now, per the instruction that an honest impossibility is better than another attempt that looks like progress but isn't.

**What's failing and why:** `npm run test:e2e -- --project=conversation-practice` fails 4 of 7 tests. All 4 live in `e2e/conversation-practice.spec.ts` and `e2e/conversation-practice-fail.spec.ts` — neither file is in task 3.2's `covers`. Each seeds a learner with vocabulary but **zero grammar cards**, then expects to reach the live recording UI. Task 3.2's own AC6 requires exactly the opposite for such a learner: the page must show the locked explanation, never the live UI. My code is correctly satisfying AC6 (proven by real red/green mutation on the identical branch), and that correctness is what makes those other files' unseeded/under-seeded learners now see the lock screen instead of what they expected.

**Why I can't fix it here:** the only fix is adding grammar-seeding to those two files' `seedLearnedVocabulary` calls — both outside my `covers`. Standing role rules are explicit: *"Write only within your task's `covers` scope... Do not widen your own scope, and do not silently skip the instruction."* I confirmed this isn't an oversight I'm inventing: task 3.3's own acceptance criteria (`plans/ai-conversation-practice/phase-3-multiturn-sessions-and-gating/task-3.3-multiturn-session-ui.md`, AC5) already state it will rewrite `conversation-practice.spec.ts`'s seeding for exactly this reason, sequenced after 3.2. `conversation-practice-fail.spec.ts` has no such planned fix anywhere in the plan — a real gap for whoever picks it up next.

**What would resolve it:** either (a) task 3.3 lands and updates `conversation-practice.spec.ts` as its own AC5 already promises, plus someone adds equivalent grammar-seeding to `conversation-practice-fail.spec.ts` (unowned today), or (b) a human/plan update explicitly widens a task's `covers` to include one or both files so an agent may touch them. Separately, `playwright.config.ts`'s `testMatch` also needs a fix (outside any covers I have) before `--project=conversation-practice` even picks up my own `conversation-gate.spec.ts` — verified via `--list` both times.

My own task's deliverables are complete, committed, and independently verified (unit suite 23/23 green, `tsc -b` clean, my e2e spec's two cases pass under `--project=chromium` with a real red/green mutation proof). I'm marking this run `blocked` rather than `complete`, per "you may not finish over a gate you watched go red" — the work stands as committed; only the cross-task gate resolution is what's blocked.
